 How Jamie Lynn Spears really feels about sister Britney’s latest Instagram takedown 
 By 
 Bernie Zilio 
 Published 
 Nov. 2, 2026, 11:59 a.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 
 Jamie Lynn Spears is brushing off her sister Britney Spears’ latest Instagram takedown , Page Six is told.
 An insider exclusively shared with us Monday that Jamie, 35, and her husband, Jamie Watson, “aren’t really concerned about the post,” mostly because it doesn’t ring true for them.
 “[Britney] held Ivey, and Ivey loves her,” our source insisted after the Princess of Pop claimed her sister “never let [her] hold” her and Watson’s 8-year-old daughter “one time” when she visited the family in Louisiana during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic.

 In Sunday’s scathing upload, Britney twice proclaimed she “will find a new family,” claiming they all participated in “secret things … behind [her] back.”
 The Grammy winner, 44, said “they made [her] feel like a slave,” noting that “all [she] ever did was work for [her] dad,” Jamie Spears, who oversaw her controversial 13-year conservatorship.
 Britney also took aim at her ex-husband Kevin Federline , with whom she shares sons Sean Preston Federline, 20, and Jayden James Federline, 19.

 According to the mother of two, Kevin “wouldn’t let [her] use the bathroom” in his house whenever she “would pick up [their] children.”
 The message was accompanied by a screenshot of Dakota Fanning’s precocious, emotionally guarded character in the 2003 movie “Uptown Girls,” holding up her middle finger.
 Reps for Jamie Lynn, Watson, Jamie, Kevin and Britney did not immediately respond to Page Six’s requests for comment.
 6 
 The Grammy winner (second from left) said “they made [her] feel like a slave,” noting that “all [she] ever did was work for [her] dad,” Jamie Spears (far left), who oversaw her controversial 13-year conservatorship. Corbis via Getty Images 
 6 
 Britney also took aim at her ex-husband Kevin Federline (pictured together in February 2006), with whom she shares two sons. L. Busacca 
 Since her conservatorship was completely terminated in November 2021, Britney has publicly called out her family for allegedly working her to the bone, wrongfully profiting off her success, controlling her and silencing her.
 Throughout the years, her father and his attorney have vehemently denied that the conservatorship was abusive , maintaining that all of his actions as his daughter’s conservator were legal, properly overseen by the court and done in her “best interest.”
 Jamie Lynn, for her part, has repeatedly denied playing a part in the conservatorship , addressing many of Britney’s claims in her memoir, “Things I Should Have Said: Family, Fame and Figuring it Out.”
 Kevin has also denied intentional wrongdoing via both his own memoir, “You Thought You Knew,” and his own attorney.
